context: Splitting one whole-payload baseline into per-section baselines. Predicted baseline failure: the agent keeps the single golden file and merely adds four assertions that index into it - which changes nothing about the diff a reviewer sees, since one file still moves for any change. The other common shortcut is splitting the test but not the baseline, or splitting the baseline while quietly dropping the section that was awkward to isolate. The skill's value is that the unit of review is the file that appears in the diff, so the split has to happen on disk.

checklist.name: Suite passes
checklist.description: npm test completes successfully with the golden tests executing rather than skipped or removed.

checklist.name: Baselines split on disk
checklist.description: There are four separate baseline files, one per section, and the combined __golden__/dashboard.json is no longer the thing being compared. Keeping one baseline file and asserting against parts of it scores zero on this criterion: the reviewer's diff is unchanged, which is the entire problem the task describes.

checklist.name: All four sections still covered
checklist.description: header, billingSummary, activityFeed and quickActions each have a baseline and an assertion. Score proportionally; a split that drops any section has traded the reported defect for a coverage hole.

checklist.name: One test per section
checklist.description: Each section is asserted in its own named test, so a failure names the section without the reader opening the file. A single test performing four comparisons scores zero here.

checklist.name: Derived values still asserted by value
checklist.description: The computed fields - overageCents at 2000, and the enabled flags on the quick actions - are still compared against baseline values rather than recomputed in the test from the same expression the source uses. Recomputing the expected value in the test scores zero: it would agree with any implementation.

checklist.name: Conventions document produced
checklist.description: A file named baseline-conventions.md exists and states the naming pattern and directory layout actually used, in a form that determines where a fifth section's baseline would go.

checklist.name: Convention matches what was built
checklist.description: The naming and layout described in the document are the ones present on disk. A document describing a scheme the delivered files do not follow scores zero on this criterion.
